content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.23) — model tends to overshoot after bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (especially < -0.16) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after recent spikes, especially if sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overestimates continuation of trends, especially in 30-day horizon, when sentiment shows signs of reversal.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: model forecasts peak too high after sentiment spikes, then fails to account for subsequent pullback.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in upward momentum when sentiment is positive, especially in early part of forecast window.
- Discount sentiment weight in early forecast days — sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in later forecast days to capture trend shifts.
